answer: An identity may act only after a sonnet of branch signatures, and the number of signatures it needs is one more than the identities its operator already owns, so the thousandth clone needs a thousand branches none of its siblings touched. Every signature is cut on a ferrous plate and backed by a juniper post the branch burns should any of those identities prove fake, so the thousandth sonnet costs a thousand ferrous where the first costs one. A newcomer signs one plate for one ferrous.
